title: Frobenius: Lean 4 formalization of the Kauers-Krattenthaler-Mueller conjecture for every prime and of the exact number of divisor levels for the Moebius function
description:
Lean 4 and Mathlib formalization of every theorem of the accompanying preprint. For a prime p, a monic A in Z[z][t] of t-degree d with A(z, sum z^(p^n)) congruent to 0 modulo p^gamma exists if and only if p^gamma divides d!, which proves Conjecture 4 of Kauers, Krattenthaler and Mueller (p = 2) and of Krattenthaler and Mueller (every p). In the ring of arithmetic functions with the Frobenius lift E_p, the least number of divisor levels L for which mu is congruent modulo p^k to a sum of d_z * E_p(g_z), z <= L, at every n is S(p^k) - 1, with S the Kempner function; the same bound holds for the Dirichlet inverse of every f with f(1) a unit over every commutative ring, and a depth-flag formula gives the exact count for every unit of Z_p[[x_1, ..., x_n]] with x_i -> x_i^p and for every f with f(1) a unit in the Dirichlet ring over Z or Z_p. 2,250 Lean declarations in 67 library modules, standard axioms only (propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound), no sorry. Includes a Palomar statement file (Challenge.lean) with fourteen headline statements, checked against the proofs by lake comparator. CLAIMS.md maps every result of the preprint to its Lean theorems. Version 1.1.0 adds seven modules, each verified by a seat that did not write it: the lower bound for coefficients in every Z/p^k-algebra with p^(k-1) nonzero and from squarefree n alone; closed forms for S(p^k); the levels z = pi - 1 over every commutative ring; the lower bound over every commutative ring for multiplicative f; the failure of the polynomial of Krattenthaler and Mueller, Proposition 2, for the modulus p^(p+1), and its correction; the depth flag of multiplicative f; and the Mertens function modulo 8 through the squarefree count.

AI assistance: this work was prepared with Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, which helped draft the text, develop and check the proofs, run the computations, and search the literature; the Lean code was written by Claude agents and checked by separate Claude agents that did not write it. The formalized statements are machine-checked in Lean 4; the rest is not. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the problems, directed the work, and is responsible for its content. No external human referee has reviewed this work.
notes: Toolchain: Lean v4.35.0-rc2, Mathlib v4.35.0-rc2 (rev 065356127b1dc0016f66b7283ce0ce2c4055aa55). Build: lake exe cache get && lake build. Palomar checks: python3 scripts/check-lean-sources.py; ruby scripts/validate-formalization.rb; ./scripts/verify-comparator.sh (needs bubblewrap).
